reader.requirement: During an explicit or implicit CANCEL (including the implicit one of an INITIAL program's EXIT PROGRAM and the GR4 cascade to contained programs), every file in the open mode associated with an INTERNAL file connector of the cancelled program is closed as by a CLOSE with no optional phrases, for every organization, with no USE procedure executed; EXTERNAL connectors are not closed.

reader.notes: ProgramEmitter.EmitProgramClass emits CloseFiles as CloseIfOpen over every declared file except EXTERNAL and SD; CancelNode runs it (through a transient instance when none is cached) after cascading to contained programs. The runtime close never enters generated declaratives, so no USE runs; a close failure maps to status 30 and the loop continues.

refuter.evidence: Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-201/src/q1.cob (run q1-001 at --std 85): contained program Q1C declares internal file F with FILE STATUS IS GST, GST a GLOBAL item of the container Q1 (legal: §1985:VII.2.5.3 SR2 only bars the File and Communication Sections). Q1C opens F, reads to AT END (GST=10) and exits; Q1 then executes CANCEL "Q1C". Printed 'AFTER CALL GST=10 / AFTER CANCEL GST=10'. GR10 executes 'an implicit CLOSE statement without any optional phrases' for the open file; a CLOSE updates the I-O status (§1985:VII.4.2.4 GR4) and the FILE STATUS item is 'always updated ... whenever the I-O status is updated' (§1985:VII.2.5.4 GR1), so GST must read 00 after the CANCEL. The connector itself IS closed (the reader's p10d shows that). The reader's GLOBAL-file sibling holds: Q1C opened the container's GLOBAL file GF, the CANCEL left it open ('GLOBAL FILE STILL OPEN WRITE 00'). Same output at --std 2023 (q1-002), so cause (b). Code: ProgramEmitter.EmitProgramClass emits CloseFiles as bare FileCloseIfOpen calls with no EmitStoreFileStatus (SequentialIoEmitter.EmitStoreFileStatus is the only status-item store and runs only after an emitted I/O verb); ProgramTable.CancelNode and EndInitialActivation call it. Sibling precedent: kb/Work PB749 (SORT USING/GIVING implicit I/O statements had to store the status item). kb/Work search ('implicit close' x 'file status', 'CloseFiles'): no note for this; PB5685 is the related report-active implicit-close defect. cite.py: OK §1985:X.5.3.4 GR10 'an implicit CLOSE statement without any optional phrases is executed'; OK §1985:VII.4.2.4 GR4 'causes the value of the I-O status associated with file-name-1 to be updated'; OK §1985:VII.2.5.4 GR1 'always updated to contain the value of the I-O status whenever the I-O status is updated'.
refuter.corrected: NONCONFORMING (wrong-answer, cause b): the CANCEL's implicit CLOSE closes the connector but never stores its I-O status (00) into the file's FILE STATUS item, so an item that outlives the cancelled program (a GLOBAL item of the container, a LINKAGE item, an EXTERNAL item) keeps the last explicit statement's status. Repro q1.cob: expected 'AFTER CANCEL GST=00', observed 'AFTER CANCEL GST=10'.

adjudication.reason: The implicit CLOSE of a CANCEL, and of an INITIAL program's EXIT PROGRAM, never stores an I-O status: the FILE STATUS item keeps 10 where 00 is due. I ran it. Sibling of kb/Work PB5685 (the same emitted block).
